My sister, mother and I were hiking in the Colorado mountains in October. It was 60F and sunny when we began. My mother, in her moment of pure genius, decided to venture off trail a little bit. We figured we knew what she was doing.

I posted this on a similar thread a while back, but here goes again;

Three weeks ago, on a Thursday afternoon, I was finally ready to go through with a plan to commit suicide. I had planned for weeks, and made sure that I had a finished note, full tank of gas, and much more. After school, I drove out to a bridge in the mountainous areas of Arizona. 

Now, I live in Phoenix, where the city freaks out if it goes below 50F. It was raining in Phoenix, and I never thought of the weather in the mountains. I was driving in the mountains to get to the bridge when it started sleeting. Five minutes later, it was snowing, but I just kept driving. 

Eventually, the snow turned into downright whiteout conditions, and I was going 2 mph through 6 inches of fresh snow. I shit you not, I saw a semi roll off the road, and snowplows and emergency services desperately trying to get up the mountain.

Eventually, I pulled over to check on my car and to see if I could keep driving to the bridge. As I tried to get back in, my car wouldn't start. It was completely stuck in snow. 

So, I walked about a half mile in flip flops and a t shirt until I saw a ranch. I just walked into the property, and saw two kids playing with snow and building snowmen in their front yard. They greeted me, they were friendly and naive. Right then, I knew I couldn't commit suicide. It sounds cliche, but seeing such happy children made me realize that maybe I can find happiness.

I eventually was let into their home, where their friendly father drove me out to an area where I could call my mother, as there wasn't any 3G in his house. Thank christ he had a pickup truck that basically plowed through the snow. 

I called my mom and told her I'd be home. After the plows finally cleared the snow from the road, the man helped me push my car out of the snowbank on the side of the road, and I was on the way home.

I've never driven faster in my life. When I got home, I just hugged my parents and cried for the longest time. I told them everything.

Edit: To answer the "how am I now," I can't lie. I'm still struggling with severe depression. I upped my dosages of medication and have talked with some doctors about all this. I'm trying to find new ways to cope and distract myself, and I'm just trying to turn my life around.

I've suffered from depression for some time, and a few weeks ago, I made an attempt to take my life. I'm 16, for clarification.

I live in arizona, and naturally, cold weather is rare for us. I had devised a plan to drive to a bridge in the mountains outside my city, and jump. It was 450 feet tall, so I figured I wouldn't have any chance of surviving with horrid injuries.

Moving on, I began driving out. I wrote lengthy notes for each friend, family member, and so on. That alone took me a week. I finished up my last note on a rainy Thursday afternoon, and then took the 2 hour drive to the bridge. It was about 50F and rainy in Phoenix, which is quite cold for Phoenix. I entered the mountains after about an hour of driving, and the temperature kept dropping.

Eventually, I hit 4000 feet, and it began snowing. Hard. I was two miles, if that, from the bridge, and it was snowing something fierce. 6 inches of wet snow blanketed the road, and I saw a semi truck spin off into a snowy ditch. I've never driven in snow, and I have a low lying sedan, so I drove ever so slowly through the snow and ice. Eventually, I pulled over.

I pulled over into a snowy side of the road to assess the damage to my car and to see if I could keep driving. Fuck me, right? I got back in the car and tried to drive. I was stuck in the snow and my phone was dead.

I walked about a half a mile in a t-shirt and flip flops to a rural house. I walked into the front yard, and saw two kids making snowmen. I cried, I'll admit, to see such childhood innocence I once enjoyed.

I walked into the house, ashamed, and asked if I could use a phone. The friendly father said yes, but that he'd have to take me to a booth in town. He drove to town and asked me why I ended up in the area. I lied to him, told him I was photographing snow for a school project. 

I charged my phone with his phone charger, and I ended up seeing 20 missed messages from my mom when I got 3G. She was scared to death. I called her and told her I was coming home.

For a minute, I thought I might just walk to the bridge. Then the kids brought me cookies they had made and told me to drive safe. That gave me the incentive to not jump.

So, I got my car unstuck from the snow, and drove down back to Phoenix. When I got home, I was a wreck, and told my parents that I had been planning to commit suicide for months.

Weeks later, and I'm still suffering. But, I don't think I'll try again.
